content: Fexofenadine hydrochloride is an antihistamine that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of symptoms such as a runny nose, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and itching of the nose or throat. These symptoms are typically associated with hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies. Common adverse reactions to fexofenadine hydrochloride include stomach ache, backache, dizziness, headache, drowsiness, fatigue, and pain in the limbs. For adults, the medication is indicated to temporarily relieve symptoms caused by hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies, including a runny nose, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and itching of the nose or throat. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of fexofenadine hydrochloride in adults, but it has been used for pre-treatment in hymenoptera immunotherapy and for perennial allergic rhinitis. For pediatric patients, the medication is also indicated to temporarily relieve symptoms caused by hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies, such as a runny nose, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and itching of the nose or throat. Limited information is available regarding off-label uses in pediatric patients, but it has been used for pre-treatment in hymenoptera immunotherapy and for perennial allergic rhinitis. Contraindications include a history of allergic reactions to fexofenadine hydrochloride or any of its ingredients. Patients with kidney disease should consult a doctor before use, as a different dose may be required. When using this medication, it is important not to exceed the recommended dose. It should not be taken simultaneously with aluminum or magnesium antacids, nor should it be taken with fruit juices. If an allergic reaction to the medication occurs, medical help should be sought immediately. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. The medication should be kept out of reach of children, and in the case of an overdose, medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center should be sought immediately. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include gastrointestinal issues such as stomach ache, musculoskeletal issues such as backache, and neurological symptoms such as dizziness, headache, and drowsiness. Other reported effects include fatigue and pain in the limbs. There is limited information available regarding drug interactions, use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing mothers, pediatric use, geriatric use, gender-specific populations, racial populations, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, and immunocompromised patients. Additionally, there is no established guidance on the interaction of fexofenadine hydrochloride with alcohol. The medication is administered orally. There is limited information available regarding monitoring, IV compatibility, chronic overdose, pharmacology, mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, clinical studies, storage, and patient counseling information. The interaction between alcohol and fexofenadine hydrochloride has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Fexofenadine hydrochloride is marketed under brand names such as 7 Select Allergy Relief. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for fexofenadine hydrochloride.
